source.version: Author accepted manuscript for Computers & Education, dated March 9th, 2024 (p. 1). The title page states it 'is not the copy of record' and gives the final DOI 10.1016/j.compedu.2024.105031. Posted on PsyArXiv (10.31234/osf.io/9z2tc).
source.title_on_document: ChatGPT Improves Creative Problem-Solving Performance in University Students: An Experimental Study

supplement.where: The manuscript refers to no supplementary material or online appendix. Appendix 1 (evaluation matrix, p. 40) is inside this PDF. The preregistration is at osf.io/q6wtu (p. 9).
supplement.holds: Nothing beyond the main text. All arm means, SDs, t-tests, d values (Table 2, p. 16) and ANCOVA F-tests (pp. 16-17) are in this PDF.

paper_design_summary: University students in a lab were randomly assigned to solve a Product Improvement Task (three ideas to improve a stuffed bunny so Mattel's sales beat Lego's) either with ChatGPT open in a second browser tab (77) or without it (68). Before that, both groups did an Unusual Uses Task without ChatGPT as a baseline. Two expert raters blind to condition scored each participant's solutions for quality, elaboration, and originality on 1-5 scales; self-efficacy, self-evaluations, interest, difficulty, and effort were self-reported.

studies.label: Lab experiment: Product Improvement Task with vs without ChatGPT

assignment.what_was_assigned: Condition: task resolution with ChatGPT (experimental) vs without ChatGPT (control)
assignment.quote: Male and female students who volunteered for the experiment were randomly assigned to either the control condition (task resolution without ChatGPT) or the experimental one (task resolution with ChatGPT) prior to the experiment.
assignment.prereg_locator: p. 9, end of Present Study: 'The experimental design and research hypotheses were preregistered at Open Science Framework (osf.io/q6wtu).'

arms.name: Experimental (ChatGPT)
arms.description: Solved the Product Improvement Task with ChatGPT-3.5 (Plus) open in a second browser tab, after a brief description of ChatGPT with example prompts and responses

arms.name: Control (no ChatGPT)
arms.description: Solved the same Product Improvement Task without ChatGPT; no other browser tabs open

participants.exclusions: None. The paper says all participants passed attention checks and completed all tasks, so no participants were excluded (p. 10). The paper does not give a separate count at assignment; assignment happened 'prior to the experiment', and it does not say whether any assigned volunteers failed to attend.
participants.who: University student volunteers (BA and MA; mostly social sciences and humanities) from a pool of about 8000, who received a small portion of course credit; age about 22.4-22.5 years
participants.country: not_stated (lab at the first author's institution; first author is at the Institute of Psychology, Czech Academy of Sciences, Prague)
participants.quote: The control group for the present study contained 68 university students and the experimental group contained 77 participants
participants.locator: p. 11, Participants, and Table 1 (Control N = 68, Experimental N = 77); p. 10 for no exclusions; abstract p. 2

ai_tool.how_used: ChatGPT open in a second browser tab during the Product Improvement Task; participants first read a brief description of ChatGPT with example prompts and responses and were told they could add context and ask it to regenerate responses (p. 10). Task instructions added '[With the assistance of ChatGPT,]' (p. 13).

task.description: Product Improvement Task adapted from Puente-Díaz et al. (2021): as a Mattel consultant, create three solutions, as original and as useful as possible, to improve a 30 cm stuffed bunny so that Mattel's sales exceed the Lego Group's (pp. 12-13). Baseline: Unusual Uses Task (paperclip) without ChatGPT in both conditions (p. 12).
task.duration: Whole experiment M = 26 (SD = 8) minutes in control and M = 36 (SD = 9) minutes in the experimental condition (p. 10); no time limit stated for the task

outcomes.name: PIT quality
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Two experts blind to condition, answers in randomized order; quality = extent to which answers match the goals (improve the bunny and increase sales), 1 (worst) to 5 (best); weighted kappa = .88 (p. 13; matrix in Appendix 1, p. 40). Raters for the UUT were the first and last authors (p. 12); the PIT raters are described as 'Two experts' (p. 13). Reported both as independent-samples t-test and as ANCOVA with prior ChatGPT experience as covariate.

contrasts.reported: Control M 2.99 (SD 0.86, N = 68) vs Experimental M 3.60 (SD 0.89, N = 77); t(143) = 4.16, p < .001, d = 0.69. ANCOVA: F(1,142) = 19.07, p < .001, partial eta squared = .12
contrasts.locator: p. 16, Table 2 row 4 and H1 text; Ns from p. 11, Table 1

outcomes.name: PIT elaboration
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Two experts blind to condition; elaboration = amount of detail, 1 to 5; weighted kappa = .93 (p. 13; Appendix 1, p. 40). t-test and ANCOVA with prior ChatGPT experience as covariate.

contrasts.reported: Control M 2.21 (SD 0.74, N = 68) vs Experimental M 2.79 (SD 1.11, N = 77); t(143) = 3.65, p < .001, d = 0.61. ANCOVA: F(1,142) = 14.87, p = <.001, partial eta squared = .10
contrasts.locator: p. 16, Table 2 row 5 and H1 text; Ns from p. 11, Table 1

outcomes.name: PIT originality
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Two experts blind to condition; originality = uniqueness of the ideas, 1 to 5; weighted kappa = .85 (p. 13; Appendix 1, p. 40). Variants: t-test (Table 2); ANCOVA with prior ChatGPT experience as covariate; and a group x task (UUT pre-test vs PIT) interaction on z-scored originality shown in Figure 1 with 95% CIs.

contrasts.reported: Control M 2.21 (SD 0.91, N = 68) vs Experimental M 2.74 (SD 1.02, N = 77); t(143) = 3.32, p < .001, d = 0.55. ANCOVA: F(1,142) = 12.56, p < .001, partial eta squared = .08. Pre-test (UUT) difference F(1,142) = 0.01, p = .928; interaction F(1,142) = 7.79, p = .006, partial eta squared = .05 (Figure 1, z-scores, error bars 95% CI, values only in the figure)
contrasts.locator: p. 16, Table 2 row 6 and H1 text; p. 17, Figure 1 and text; Ns from p. 11, Table 1

eligibility.reason: Students were randomly assigned to solve an idea-generation task with or without ChatGPT (p. 10); 145 people analyzed (68 control, 77 ChatGPT; no exclusions; pp. 10-11, Table 1); quality, elaboration, and originality of the solutions were scored by two blind expert raters (p. 13).

one_line_finding: Students solving the Product Improvement Task with ChatGPT produced solutions rated higher in quality (3.60 vs 2.99, d = 0.69), elaboration (2.79 vs 2.21, d = 0.61), and originality (2.74 vs 2.21, d = 0.55) than students without it (N = 77 vs 68; p. 16, Table 2).
open_questions: Control and experimental groups had separate sessions of up to five participants (p. 10). Assignment was individual, but outcomes may cluster by session; the paper's tests treat participants as independent.
The paper does not say whether any volunteers were randomized but did not attend, so the count at assignment is not stated; 145 is the analyzed count with no exclusions.
The paper does not label any of H1a-c (or the other hypotheses) as the primary outcome; the preregistration (osf.io/q6wtu) was not checked.
This is the accepted manuscript; the published version may add a data availability statement or other material not in this PDF.
The rubric in Appendix 1 does not say whether one score covers all three solutions or each solution is scored and averaged; t(143) implies one score per participant.
notes: Not listed as outcomes: the Unusual Uses Task originality (a pre-treatment baseline done without ChatGPT in both arms; Control 1.74 SD 0.99 vs Experimental 1.71 SD 0.81, t = 0.18, p = .855, d = 0.03; Table 2 row 1, p. 16), and all self-reports (self-efficacy, self-evaluations of quality and originality, bias indices, interest, difficulty, effort, usefulness of ChatGPT; Table 2 rows 2-3 and 7-14). The bias indices combine self-evaluations with rated performance and are not creativity scores. Students could use the web browser for other tools in both conditions, but the paper says no one did (p. 10). Prior ChatGPT experience correlates with PIT quality, elaboration, and originality in the experimental group (Table 3, p. 18). PDF page numbers equal the printed page numbers.
